Sasha: Quick heads-up: weird p99 spikes in the replay harness when we switch kernel selection heuristics. baseline vs new kernel shows ~30% tail increase. anyone seen socket-priming + TLS + Nagle interactions? :eyes:

Matt: Saw something similar last week. Our replays with short-lived connections + HTTP/1.1 had worse tails. gRPC (http/2) runs looked better because of multiplexing, but it's not a drop-in comparison.

Jen: What exactly is your harness config? conn reuse? keepalive? batch sizes? KV cache warm state?

Sasha: Replay harness used: ```./replay --conn=200 --rate=300/s --keepalive=false --warmup=30s --seq-hist=short-heavy --model=v1.2```
We compared kernel=binary_old vs kernel=binary_new. New one picks a matmul kernel optimized for long sequences — faster on big batches but small-batch path latency increased. Also KV cache warm fraction was low (~20%).

Ryan: That mix explains it: kernel selection depends on observed sequence-length distribution. If the replay over-indexes short sequences, the runtime chooses a different kernel and batching heuristics kick in differently. Also client-side fact: disabling keepalive forces TCP+TLS handshake per request -> huge tail.

Carmen: For TLS + Nagle we saw an extra 1-2ms per request when sockets weren't primed. We fixed it by: 1) setting TCP_NODELAY on the client, 2) pre-opening connections in the pool, 3) increasing SO_SNDBUF for the client sockets to avoid TCP aggregation forcing small writes.

Matt: Recommend a concrete apples-to-apples methodology: 1) match sequence-length histogram between baseline and experiment, 2) prefill KV cache with common prefixes, 3) warmup for 2x normal to let kernel selection stabilize, 4) use long-lived connections or gRPC with equivalent stream limits. Also use eBPF + perf to correlate p99 spikes with syscall durations.

bench-bot: Benchmark run 2076543200 finished. p50=45ms, p95=220ms, p99=410ms. config: kernel=new, keepalive=false, conn=200.

Sasha: Did a follow-up with --keepalive=true --pool=50 and TCP_NODELAY=true; p99 dropped from 410ms -> 180ms. Will add that to the standard template. :thumbsup:

Jen: Also log kernel selection per request. You can enable REDWOOD_KERNTRACE=1 or attach `perf record` to the worker to capture which kernel path was used. We need per-request kernel id in the bench trace for correlation.

Ryan: Note about gRPC vs REST: gRPC amortizes TLS handshake across streams but has stream limits per connection. For apples-to-apples, match concurrency PER CONNECTION, not just global RPS. Otherwise multiplexing hides other client bottlenecks.

Carmen: For reproducible replays, snapshot client connection warm state: e.g., run a priming phase that opens and warms all client pools for 5-15s, then zero telemetry counters and start the measured run. That avoids TCP slow-start and TLS handshake noise in the measured window.

Sasha: Plan: update replay harness to add flags: --priming=true --priming-duration=10s --prefill-kv=/tmp/kv_seeds.json and a `--emit-kerntrace` that stamps kernel id per request in the event log. Will rerun and post results.

Matt: Also add a lightweight perf-regression check in CI: compare per-token GPU time vs syscall/network time. Regressions that look like "slower model kernel" should show GPU time increases; if syscalls spike, it's client or kernel-selection behavior.

bench-bot: Created PERF-788: "Investigate kernel-selection tail regression + default keepalive off in replay harness". cc @Sasha @Matt

Sasha: Thanks all — pushing the harness change now, will drop a summary with traces and before/after p99 numbers once finished.
